<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **34** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-source-admission.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`  _(via knowledgeSources (literal, a string literal in knowledge_source; a string literal in relevantWhen; a string literal in validateKnowledgeSource), metadataFields (literal, a string literal in validateKnowledgeSource))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object), runtimeTypes (symbol, a field of const object AUTHORING_RULES))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/quick-reference.mdx`  _(via knowledge_source (symbol, a field of const object TYPE_TO_STACK_KEY), knowledge_source (literal, a string literal in runtimeTypes))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via admitAuthoredSource (symbol, a method of class KnowledgeService), isSystemObjectName (symbol, a top-level const), knowledge_source (symbol, a field of const object TYPE_TO_STACK_KEY), knowledge_source (literal, a string literal in runtimeTypes))_
- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via knowledge_source (symbol, a field of const object TYPE_TO_STACK_KEY), knowledgeSources (literal, a string literal in knowledge_source; a string literal in relevantWhen; a string literal in validateKnowledgeSource), knowledge_source (literal, a string literal in runtimeTypes), metadataFields (literal, a string literal in validateKnowledgeSource))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-source-admission.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **13** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6e2a8f2bb577b9fff5225a1280bc6cbbea680c7c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8b29383c9d57663a26ef9ee1c6d5a8cbac684e37` — the merge of head `80a26dfbc5c5794a7e87fc02800fd7547d91e2e5` into base `6e2a8f2bb577b9fff5225a1280bc6cbbea680c7c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8b29383c9d57663a26ef9ee1c6d5a8cbac684e37 && git checkout 8b29383c9d57663a26ef9ee1c6d5a8cbac684e37
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6e2a8f2bb577b9fff5225a1280bc6cbbea680c7c 80a26dfbc5c5794a7e87fc02800fd7547d91e2e5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6e2a8f2bb577b9fff5225a1280bc6cbbea680c7c && git merge --no-ff 80a26dfbc5c5794a7e87fc02800fd7547d91e2e5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6e2a8f2bb577b9fff5225a1280bc6cbbea680c7c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6e2a8f2bb577b9fff5225a1280bc6cbbea680c7c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `80a26dfbc5c5794a7e87fc02800fd7547d91e2e5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/19.knowledge-source-publish-refuses-missing-references-and-gated-objects.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-knowledge-source.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-knowledge-source.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-ai-context.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-ai-context.test.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-source-admission.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/__tests__/knowledge-source-admission.test.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/semantic-relevance.test.ts + read in the cited code, never reviewed: docs/adr/0161 (K4, on main), packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts, packages/lint/src/system-fields.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-object-references.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-list-view-field-refs.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-package-addressing.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts, packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, the four sibling 19.knowledge-source-* entries, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs

Stacked PR. The branch carries PR #37971 at 830150985dc08854ae7c5e59e7e2878b9a181a67, whose commits are covered by its own records (7221784031, then 7224039424 on that head). This record judges the one commit 80a26dfbc5 (`git diff 830150985d 80a26dfbc5`, 11 files, +150/-24), reading #37971's state as the base. The first Scope path is the one `reviewFace` returns as a hit on the file list (a non-test path under `packages/spec/src`); the rest is the narrowing floor, every non-prose path of the delta. The changeset is read, not reviewed.

Inputs read: card #38019 body and its three comments (triage 7224148251, claim 7224310710, dev report 7226457832), card #37307, PR #38038 body and comments, records 7221784031 and 7224039424 and seat ruling 7221816104 on #37971, and the check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Accept set of the runtime publish door for `knowledge_source`, a write that names no package (the whole collection): narrower. A `source.object` that is a platform-prefixed name no known package registers (was a warning on the 2xx), or a known platform name (`sys_user`) the host does not serve (was not judged), is now `knowledge-source-object-unknown`, error, 422. Two conditions, both `!whole &&`, on the two platform rungs; `whole` is `!closure && options.wholeCollection === true`, the same expression the list-view member computes (validate-list-view-field-refs.ts:1215). Right, and it is the declared narrowing.
2. Accept set of the door under a stated package closure: unchanged. The known-platform skip still runs first and the closure arm still refuses everything else. Right as a statement of the delta; see N1.
3. Accept set of `os validate` / `lint` / `compile` / `build` for knowledge sources: unchanged. The CLI sets neither option, so `whole` is false and both platform rungs read as before. Pinned in the new test (warning for `sys_kb_article`, nothing for `sys_user`). Right.
4. Empty whole collection: unchanged. `noUniverse` is tested before either platform rung, so a failed registry read with no stored object row still judges nothing. Right.
5. `ai_context` findings: one false warning removed. A field named `id` in `fields`, a related list's `fields`, `where`, `orderBy` and `body.field` now resolves through `injectedColumnsFor`, the helper `system-fields.ts` names for an existence question; the definition map still answers the type questions. `body.field: 'id'` falls to `ai-context-body-not-long-text` because `def` is undefined and `str(def?.type)` is empty. The rule's registry entry is `tier: 'advisory'`, so no publish verdict moves and default `os validate` exit status does not move. Under `--strict`, where a warning fails the run, a pack naming `id` now passes: a false refusal removed, not a new capability. Right; the PR's stated reason is incomplete, see N3.
6. Text of the `object-api-not-served` save refusal (403 PERMISSION_DENIED from `admitAuthoredSource`): cause and fix reworded; code, status and the deciding predicate (`canServeApiOperation(enable, 'search')`) untouched. No accept set moves. Right.
7. `os migrate meta` default listing: the entry `knowledge-source-publish-refuses-missing-references-and-gated-objects` is counted, not listed, for a stack that provably declares no `knowledgeSources`; `--all` lists it. No accept set and no export moves. Right.
8. Public surface of the three packages: no export added, removed or re-typed. `fieldExists` and `addressable` are locals of `validateAiContext`; `relevantWhen` is an existing optional field of `SemanticMigration`. Right.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/lint` minor with the BREAKING banner: right. The narrowing lives in lint and a kind other than `none` takes at least minor on a package the diff moves. `@objectstack/service-knowledge` patch: right, one message string and a header comment. `@objectstack/spec` patch: right, an entry's `surface` prose and its relevance question; no schema, no key, no export; it matches the level #37971 and the sibling entry-only changesets took. `Check Changeset` is green on the head. The FROM and TO sentence and the one-line fix are in the body.

`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`: right. The criterion is whether the card widens a published accept set or enlarges the public surface. Item 3 only refuses. Item 2 removes a refusal the published contract already denies (`id` exists on every object: `injected-system-columns.ts` names it the driver's primary key and `system-fields.ts` reports it from `injectedColumnsFor`), and the standing rule reads that as `no` when the text is cited. Nothing is exported. `yes` on #37971 rested on its new exports, which this commit does not add.

`Metadata-protocol: narrowed`: right. A value an author could publish is now refused, which is the definition's own wording. The claim comment carried `none`; the diff decides, and the dev report states the change.

`Skills-docs: follow-up #37310`: the card exists and is open.

ADR-0087 marker. It reads `registered knowledge-source-publish-refuses-missing-references-and-gated-objects`. That is the only spelling the gate admits on this head: against `main` the diff still adds the entry (it arrives with #37971's commit), and `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` refuses `already-registered` when it names only ids the diff adds. Once #37971 merges and `main` is merged here, the same gate refuses `registered` because no id is new in the diff, and prints the line to write: `not-required (already-registered ID) why`. So the flip is owed, it is gate-enforced, and it cannot be skipped silently. Acceptable now. It is a changeset edit, so it moves the head: this record does not cover that head, and the edit is a release-text-only change of the kind the seat confirms on ACCEPT. The entry does cover the new refusal: its `surface` names `knowledge-source-object-unknown` at the publish gate and now says the platform-name warning is the CLI's.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question, N6 scope (one entry or all five). Answer: A, one entry. `SemanticMigration.relevantWhen` says to omit the question unless the surface lives ONLY under the top-level keys it names. Read in the tree: `19.knowledge-source-content-lists-fields` and `19.knowledge-source-inert-keys-retired` name "a source registered in code"; `19.knowledge-source-file-http-kinds-retired` names host code calling `indexDocument` or `deleteDocument`; `19.knowledge-source-registration-governed` is about the code door alone. A stack with no `knowledgeSources` is not proven clear of any of the four, and a question that hid them would be the silent miss ADR-0087 D3 forbids. The one entry that carries the question qualifies: its rule reads `stack.knowledgeSources` and judges nothing registered in code, and runtime-stored metadata is outside the proof by the type's own contract. `knowledgeSources` is a `StackDefinitionKey` (stack.zod.ts:1235), and the enumeration table and counts in `semantic-relevance.test.ts` are updated in the same commit. B would need a ruling that amends the contract. Consequence for the card: acceptance bullet 4 ("the knowledge-source upgrade entries are listed only for a stack that declares knowledge sources") is met for one entry of five by design. That is a narrowing of the card's text, stated in the PR and the report; the seat's ACCEPT should say so on the card.
- Deviation, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` where the claim carried `none`. Right, see ②.
- Deviation, ADR-0087 marker. Answered in ②.
- Deviation, PR body Tests section reads NOT MEASURED. The dev report 7226457832 supersedes it with measured runs at this head. The body should be aligned (N5); a PR-body edit moves no head.
- Dogfood battery: NOT MEASURED locally. The dev report gives the reason (the shared verification lock; about 55 minutes of battery). The `(narrowing)` arm owes it, and it is carried by the queue's Dogfood Regression Gate before merge. The check-run of that name on this pull-request head reports success; the merge-group run is the one that counts. Not measured by this review either.
- Check-runs on the head, read at review time: 56 success, 10 skipped, 1 in progress (`Test Core (6/10)`), 2 failed (`Type Check · workspace` and its rollup `TypeScript Type Check`). The failed job's log holds no compiler error: it ends in "The runner has received a shutdown signal" and "The operation was canceled" at 19:21Z. So the type-check gate has given no verdict on this head. The dev report records local typecheck of the three packages at exit 0, which is the dev's reading, not the gate's. This record's verdict is on the contract; the job must be re-run and be green, and the last Test Core shard must finish green, before the PR is queued. Neither moves the head.
- Branch name is `claude/area-o1C-38019` as the claim comment states. No finding.
- Security-touching: no. The rule only adds a refusal; the admission predicates and the search-time gate are untouched; the reworded message discloses nothing new (the object name was already in it).
- SQL push-down: no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join is added. The gate's per-write collection read is unchanged.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec. ADR-0161 K4 on main says a `knowledge_source` item "is refused when the object or a named field does not exist". Seat ruling 7221816104 on #37971 applies it: the publish door refuses. The base head left one leak, named N3 in both #37971 records: with the whole host universe in hand, an absent platform name passed (a skip, or a warning). This commit closes it. No declared capability is taken away at the consumer: a source over an object the host does not serve indexes nothing and no search returns a hit from it, so what was accepted was a source that could not work. The spec's own refusal is made real.

Tried to break it: can a legitimately served platform object be refused?

- Is the universe really every served object? The gate reads `engine.registry.listItems('object')`, which for the object type returns `getAllObjects()` with no package filter and no disabled-package filter (registry-package-addressing.ts:745-752), then folds the stored `sys_metadata` object rows on top. A platform object registered by any plugin, optional or not, first-party or third-party, is in that list once registered. The knowledge service reads schemas from the same registry, so a name absent here has no schema there either.
- An optional plugin not loaded. Its objects are absent, the source would index nothing, and the refusal is correct. The hint names the remedy (install the package that registers it).
- A disabled package. Its objects stay in `getAllObjects`, so the lint rule does not refuse; the save door's own disabled-package gate does. No false refusal from this change.
- `cloud_` and `ai_` names. They take the same path. An environment kernel that does not register a `cloud_` object cannot index it, so the refusal is correct there.
- Timing. The gate runs on an `active` publish only; a draft pays nothing. A `migrate-stored` pass returns clean before any collection is read, and stored rows are not judged at boot, so no existing source is refused by an upgrade; the next publish of it is, which the changeset states. The `package-author` channel (the control-plane bootstrap kernel) returns clean before the rules run, so a kernel that holds no environment objects does not judge. Code-package metadata loads into the registry without passing this door. A publish batch that carries the object with the source merges the pending object into the snapshot before the rule runs, exactly as for an unprefixed name.
- A packaged write whose package the registry does not know resolves no scope and is judged against the whole collection. That path already existed for unprefixed names on the base head; platform objects are registered by their plugins independently of the writing package, so this change adds no refusal there that is not true.
- A partial universe. If the registry read throws, or the engine has no `listItems`, while stored object rows exist, the snapshot is non-empty and holds only tenant-authored objects. A platform object is then absent and is now refused, where it was skipped before. This is the same degenerate state in which every packaged, unprefixed object and every list view over one is already refused (#24668), and the gate's own comment places it at a metadata-only test double. Accepted as the standing reading; not a finding of this delta.
- A served object under a different key. The lookup is by `name` over the listed objects, the same key the unprefixed rung and the field rungs use. No alias path is new.

Not broken. Every refusal the new condition produces is of a name the host does not serve.

Consistency with the siblings. The list-view member never consulted the platform-name predicates under the whole collection, so a list view over an absent `sys_user` is already refused there. The knowledge-source rule now reads the same way. `validateObjectReferences` keeps its ladder at every site; that is its own contract and outside this card.

Item 1, wording. The shipped text is the card's sentence, cause and fix, character for character, and it is the wording #37971's rule message carries (validate-knowledge-source.ts:287-292). It agrees with `canServeApiOperation`: `apiEnabled: false` refuses; a list without `list` refuses; `list` beside `searchable: false` refuses; the fix is conditioned on "where it declares `enable.apiMethods`", which is the predicate's own condition. The phrase "for `search`" names the operation, not a list value. No other string in `service-knowledge` prescribes a `search` grant. The new pin covers all three not-served shapes and adds the `list` + `searchable: false` row to the refusal table.

Item 2, `ai_context`. All five existence sites now ask `fieldExists`. After a positive answer no site dereferences a definition that may be missing: the body branch uses `def?.type`, the unprovisioned-body branch is guarded by `def &&`, sortability reads `sortability[name]` with optional chaining, and the link search reads `referenceOf(childFields.get(name))` only over declared keys. The control (a misspelling `idd`) still reports. The `owner_id` under `ownership: 'org'` pin beside it still holds, because `injectedColumnsFor` reads the same plan the definition map does.

Item 4. Judged in ③: rule A is the contract's reading.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

N1 (nit) — under a stated closure an absent known platform name is still skipped. The closure keeps every system object unconditionally (runtime-gate.ts, limb 1), so for a `sys_` name the snapshot is as final there as the whole collection is, and a packaged publish is the common path for a packaged source. The card and the earlier N3 scoped the fix to the whole collection, and the commit does what the card says. The remaining K4 leniency is a follow-up card, one condition on the same rung, with the question of `cloud_` and `ai_` names (which limb 1 may not keep) stated in it.

N2 (nit) — the rule header says the two platform arms apply "both on the CLI and under a closure". Under a closure only the first does: a platform-prefixed name no known package registers reaches the closure arm and is an error with the dependency remedy, never the warning. The `os explain` text has the mirror slip: it places the not-judged arm "on the command line" only, though it also holds under a closure. Verdicts are unaffected. Fix with N1's follow-up; an edit here moves the head.

N3 (nit) — the PR body says item 2 leaves the accept set of `os validate` unchanged because every `ai_context` finding is a warning. Under `--strict` a warning fails the run, so a pack naming `id` is newly accepted there. The `no` stands by the other rule: removing a refusal the published contract already denies is `no`, with the text cited. The body should give that reason and cite `injected-system-columns.ts` (the driver's primary key) and `system-fields.ts`. PR-body edit only.

N4 (nit) — a `body.field` of `id` reads "names 'id', a untyped field". The rule id is right and pinned; the sentence could say what `id` is (the record's primary key). Cosmetic; follow-up or leave.

N5 (nit) — the PR body's Tests section still reads NOT MEASURED while the dev report carries measured runs and an ablation at this head. The seat aligns the body, as the report asks.

N6 (nit) — at a write that names no package the refusal says "which this stack does not define" and the hint offers "declare that package in the manifest's `dependencies`". Both are inherited from the unprefixed arm of the base head and neither is wrong enough to mislead ("install it" is the working half), but a tenant author has no stack and no manifest. Fold into N1's follow-up.

Owed before queueing, none of it a change to this head: a green re-run of `Type Check · workspace`, a green finish of `Test Core (6/10)`, and, after #37971 lands and `main` is merged, the ADR-0087 marker edit and the Dogfood Regression Gate on that final head.

## 席位核对

**Shape.** The PR is stacked on #37971 at 830150985d, whose commits are covered by that PR's own records. This verdict judges the one commit 80a26dfbc5 (11 files, +150/-24). `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` · `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`.

**Contract review.** Record 7226609684 at this head: PASS at the contract tier (`verify-review-tier` PASS), `No must-fix, no should-fix.`, six nits. I adopt it.
- **Item 3, the narrowing.** It holds against ADR-0161 K4 and seat ruling 7221816104. The gate reads the whole registered object collection, which includes optional and third-party plugins, plus stored rows. Only an `active` publish is judged.
- **N6 scope.** Rule A, `relevantWhen` on the one entry, is right under the `types.ts` contract. Card acceptance bullet 4 is met for that one entry, and the seat's record should say so.
- **The ADR-0087 marker** `registered` is correct while the diff still adds the entry. It must become `not-required (already-registered ID) why` once #37971 lands and main is merged. That edit moves the head, so it needs a delta L2 and a delta L1.

**Before the seat's handoff.**
- `Type Check · workspace` and its rollup `TypeScript Type Check` are red at this head. The log shows no compiler error; the runner was shut down at 19:21Z. Re-run it, and wait for it and Test Core (6/10) to go green.
- Dogfood is owed on the narrowing. It is NOT MEASURED locally, and the queue's Dogfood Regression Gate carries it as declared.
- In practice the landing head comes after #37971 merges, with the marker flip, so the handoff follows that head's delta.

**Nits, PR-body or follow-up.** N3: the body's item-2 accept-set sentence, which differs under `--strict`. N5: the stale Tests section. N1 and N6 can go together as a follow-up card on the closure arm. N2 and N4 are prose.

**Landing:** narrowing, so it goes through the seat's Tier H handoff.

`Type Check · workspace` (job 140690857398, run 46053662926) and its `TypeScript Type Check` rollup are red with no compiler error: the log ends at `@objectstack/plugin-dev`'s typecheck (`ELIFECYCLE Command failed.`, 130 of 142 tasks successful) immediately followed by `##[error]The operation was canceled.`, the sole failure annotation. `plugin-dev` is outside this PR's diff and no task printed a `tsc` diagnostic, so the job was stopped, not failed by the code. One re-run of the failed jobs; a second red on this job is read as real.
